title: Asset budgets per destination in Rust: fewer and smaller files, later groups, import facts read
note: Fit web 64 MB, phones 200 MB and desktop 2 GB of assets; shrink and drop files before raising [assets] budget_mb; later content goes in an [[asset_group]].
intent: Every destination measures its package against an asset budget: 64 MB on the web, 200 MB on an iPhone or Android phone, 2 GB on a desktop. Past it an export still ships with assets-over-budget and downloads slower; past the hard cap (512 MB on the web, 4096 MB on a phone) the build is refused assets-over-ceiling. Fit the budget before raising [assets] budget_mb: fetch textures at the size they are seen at (1k on phones), reuse one material across props, let phones keep textures up to phone_max_texture_px (2048 by default) and remove files the game never loads. Read genex-assets.lock after each delivery: a row's issues name triangles-over-budget (a character over 100,000 triangles, any other model over 250,000), albedo-out-of-range or metallic-partial by code; fix the model, never the lock, which Studio alone writes. Assets the first frame does not need (a second level, a castle's interiors) go in an [[asset_group]] so they arrive while playing, not before the first frame; a reset never reads one (not-preloaded).
sketch:
# genex.toml
[assets]
phone_max_texture_px = 1024    # a phone-first game: halve every phone texture

[assets.desktop]
budget_mb = 1024               # only when the brief is desktop-first and the files are already lean

[[asset_group]]
name = "castle"
paths = ["interiors/castle/**", "props/throne.glb"]
port: The facet that owns a level owns its asset group; the budget keys are the game's, changed only with the reason in the facet's notes.

evidence.note: [assets] budget_mb and phone_max_texture_px, assets-over-budget, assets-over-ceiling, [[asset_group]] globs.
A reset reads boot and sim group assets only; a named group refuses not-preloaded.
